headline: Doctorow AI批判書評
context: 科幻作家 Cory Doctorow 的新書《The Reverse Centaur's Guide to Life After AI》評論出爐，被形容為對 AI 時代科技業「充滿怒火」的政治經濟觀察。書評提到前谷歌執行長 Eric Schmidt 在大學畢業典禮上替 AI 造勢卻遭學生噓場的場景。倫敦日本館（Japan House）同期有免費攝影展，將廣島核爆後的廢墟景象與淒美的日本花景並排展出。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: A vivid and entertaining polemic on the economics of the tech revolution, filled with righteous ire As former Google CEO Eric Schmidt could tell you, AI is a hard sell these days. Last month, he tried talking up the AI revolution during a commencement address at the University of Arizona and was loudly booed by students about to enter an AI-ravaged job market. His discombobulation was telling. Schmidt is not the only AI booster to crash out with students recently as the popular backlash grows. Every week brings a new story about some writer, publisher or academic who has torched their reputation by using an unreliable chatbot. Most US voters are opposed to the construction of vast, resource-guzzling new datacentres. A majority believe AI will negatively impact not just jobs but creativity and human relationships. In some quarters, saying that AI has any benefits at all is akin to saying that biological warfare gets a bad rap. As a New York Times column put it : “AI populism is here. And no one is ready.” Continue reading...

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Japan House, London This darkly atmospheric exhibition pairs the revolutionary Hiroshima images of revered photographer Kikuji with Ai’s glittering but deeply melancholy visions of cherry blossom Japan House’s first, free photography exhibition, Kyotographie: Kawada Kikuji x Iwane Ai begins with slow-burning suggestions of fire: a box of Lucky Strike cigarettes, its surface crackling and curled; Coca-Cola bottles sinking into a dark bed of crushed ashes. Kawada took the photographs with a 4x5 plate camera; here they’re reprinted on washi paper, the textures and density of the blackness making them even more evocative of obliteration. They are vestiges of American culture in the wake of American violence – images found in the wreckage of Hiroshima in the aftermath of atomic destruction. Kawada, now 93, is a photo geek’s photographer; people have paid up to £25,000 for a copy of Chizu (The Map), the photobook that collects together his tense, ruminative Hiroshima impressions , made when he was in his 20s. A series of seemingly abstract images depicts the stains on the wall – all that remained of bodies in the Genbaku (A-Bomb) Dome. Kawada was 12 when the atomic bomb hit Hiroshima. His approach to capturing one of the worst scenes of mass destruction in human history was to tell it with a kind of detachment, indirect and impressionistic, fragmented. It’s a story about proximity to trauma and surviving it. His photographs veer away from truth. The reality is impossible to comprehend – for both Kawada standing there, and us viewing the images. These were revolutionary photographs at the time – and they still feel new in their search to express the inexpressible. Continue reading...
sources.title: Kyotographie: Kawada Kikuji x Iwane Ai review – staggering images of the aftermath of shattering violence

thread_text:
書評推薦了 Cory Doctorow 的新書《The Reverse Centaur's Guide to Life After AI》。這是一本對 AI 革命的政治經濟批判，評論形容充滿怒火。書評提到一個場景：前谷歌執行長 Eric Schmidt 在亞利桑那大學（University of Arizona）畢業典禮上替 AI 造勢，結果被台下學生大聲嗆聲——書裡對這類科技業宣傳話語有直接的批評。

另外，倫敦日本館（Japan House）正在免費展出攝影展「Kyotographie: Kawada Kikuji x Iwane Ai」，把廣島核爆後的廢墟影像與攝影師岩根愛（Iwane Ai）的淒美日本景色對置，氛圍深沉。

—— 本則整理自 The Guardian，2026 年 06 月 22 日，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
threads_text:
書評推薦了科幻作家 Cory Doctorow 的新書《The Reverse Centaur's Guide to Life After AI》——一本對 AI 經濟衝擊充滿怒火的政治觀察。書評提到一個細節：前谷歌執行長 Eric Schmidt 在亞利桑那大學（University of Arizona）畢業典禮上為 AI 說話，被台下學生大聲嗆聲。

攝影展的這邊，倫敦日本館（Japan House）正在免費展出「Kyotographie: Kawada Kikuji x Iwane Ai」。這個展把日本攝影師川田喜久治（Kawada Kikuji）的廣島核爆後景象，與岩根愛（Iwane Ai）拍攝的淒美日本花景並排，評論說整個展覽氛圍深沉。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 06 月 22 日發佈的報導。
voice_text: Doctorow 新書批了 AI 革命的真實代價。書名是《The Reverse Centaur's Guide to Life After AI》，評論形容充滿怒火。書裡有一個場景，前谷歌執行長 Eric Schmidt 在大學畢業典禮上替 AI 造勢，被台下即將進入就業市場的學生大聲嗆聲。倫敦日本館有個免費攝影展，把廣島核爆後的廢墟影像，跟攝影師岩根愛拍的淒美日本景色對置，氛圍深沉。
